literal: Bearing completely the burden when it comes upon it, and paying completely the tax to the ruler, is a country.
translation: A true country is one that bears the entire burden when extra weight comes upon it, and pays its taxes fully to the ruler.
modern: கூடுதல் சுமை தன்மேல் வரும்போது அதை முழுமையாகத் தாங்கிக்கொண்டு, அரசனுக்குச் செலுத்த வேண்டிய வரிகளையும் முழுமையாகச் செலுத்துவதே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the economic and social resilience of a great nation. A true country must have the capacity to bear sudden, heavy burdens—such as supporting refugees or surviving natural disasters—without collapsing. At the same time, its citizens must remain prosperous enough to pay their taxes and dues fully to the sovereign. The word 'poṟai' refers to the external or unexpected burdens, while 'iṟai' refers to the regular taxes paid to the ruler.
